questions.q: A shop alarm sounds when the shop is closed AND a door is opened. Which expression describes it?
questions.feedback: Both conditions have to be true, which is AND.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 3 — Circuit workshop, station 1: From words to logic

questions.q: A greenhouse heater turns on when the temperature is low AND the window is not open. Which expression describes it?
questions.feedback: 'Not open' is NOT applied to Open; both conditions are needed, so AND.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 3 — Circuit workshop, station 1: From words to logic

questions.q: A hospital lift will only move when the doors are closed and either the inside button or the outside button has been pressed. Write a Boolean expression for this, and explain what each operator does.

markPoints.concept: both the door condition and a button are required
accept: both|as well as|at the same time|all of|two conditions|requires both|every condition|together|parts to hold
markPoints.exemplar: The doors must be closed as well as a button being pressed.

markPoints.concept: either button on its own is enough
accept: either|one of|at least one|any of the|one button|just one|whichever|it does not matter which
markPoints.exemplar: Either of the two buttons will do on its own.

markPoints.concept: and the OR is bracketed, so it is worked out before the AND
markPoints.exemplar: The OR is in brackets so that it is worked out before the AND.

questions.example: Q = Closed AND (Inside OR Outside). The AND means the doors must be closed as well as a button being pressed; the OR means either button will do; and the brackets make sure the OR is worked out first, so that the lift cannot move with the doors open just because a button was pressed.
questions.paraphrase: Writing it as Closed AND (Inside OR Outside): the AND requires both parts to hold, the OR accepts either button, and the brackets are there so that the button test is worked out first.
questions.feedback: What each operator requires, and what the brackets do. The brackets are the mark most answers miss, and without them the expression means something else.
questions.hint: Which part has to be worked out first for the expression to mean what the question says?
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 3 — Circuit workshop, station 1: From words to logic

questions.q: A security light comes on when it is dark AND movement is detected. Sort each situation by whether the light comes on.
questions.feedback: AND needs both. Only the first row has both.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 3 — Circuit workshop, station 1: From words to logic

questions.q: In the expression Q = A OR B AND C, the AND is worked out before the OR.
questions.feedback: True. AND binds more tightly than OR, which is why brackets are used to make the intention clear.
questions.revisitLabel: 2.4 Lesson 3 — Circuit workshop, station 1: From words to logic

questions.q: A fan turns on when the room is hot AND the window is closed. Using H for hot and W for the window being open, which expression is right?
questions.feedback: W stands for the window being OPEN, so 'closed' has to be written NOT W. Reading what each letter actually means is where most marks are lost.

questions.q: A door unlocks when a valid card is presented OR the fire alarm is sounding. Using C and F, which expression is right?
questions.feedback: Either condition on its own is enough, which is OR. A fire alarm that needed a card as well would be a dangerous door.

questions.q: A machine starts when the guard is closed AND either the green button OR the foot pedal is pressed. Using G, B and P, which expression is right?
options: Q = G AND B OR P
questions.feedback: The brackets are what make the guard compulsory. Without them the machine could start on the pedal alone with the guard open.

questions.q: A till gives a discount when the customer has a loyalty card AND is either a student OR over 65. Explain why the expression needs brackets.

markPoints.concept: the card is needed in every case
markPoints.exemplar: The loyalty card is needed whichever of the other two applies.

markPoints.concept: so the OR has to be worked out first and then combined with the card
accept: brackets make|brackets mean|brackets force|brackets group|inside the brackets|happen first|happens first|worked out first|evaluated first|done first|grouped|group|together|combined with the card|before being combined
markPoints.exemplar: So the OR must be worked out first, and its result combined with the card by the AND.

questions.example: The loyalty card is needed in every case, and the student-or-over-65 test is a choice between two ways of qualifying. The brackets make the OR happen first, so its result is then ANDed with the card. Without them, AND binds tighter than OR and somebody over 65 with no card would get the discount.
questions.paraphrase: Because the card is required whichever of the two other conditions applies, those two must be grouped and evaluated together before being combined with the card.
questions.feedback: What is always required, and what the brackets therefore have to group.
questions.hint: What would happen without the brackets, for somebody over 65 and no card?

questions.q: A circuit takes inputs A and B. A goes into a NOT gate, and the result goes into an AND gate with B. When is the output 1?
options: When A is 0 and B is 1
When A is 1 and B is 1
When A is 0 and B is 0
When A is 1 and B is 0
questions.feedback: The NOT turns A round first, so the AND sees NOT A and B — and an AND needs both of the things it is given to be 1.

questions.q: A circuit computes Q = NOT A AND B. Sort each pair of inputs by what Q is.
questions.feedback: Only one of the four rows gives 1. Inverting A first is what moves it there from the row an ordinary AND would pick.
